# Heart rate recovery: 7.5-minute recording {#sec-hrr-short}

```{r hrr-short-packages}
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
```

## Data import and exploration {#sec-hrr-short-data}

The recording is downloaded from the public Aidlab datasets (<https://www.aidlab.com/datasets>) into a `data/` folder, which is ignored by Git.

```{r hrr-short-download}
url_short <- "https://aidlab-production-datasets.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/datasets_2026-09-27_cardio_recovery_7m30s.zip"
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
zip_short <- "data/cardio_recovery_7m30s.zip"
if (!file.exists(zip_short)) download.file(url_short, zip_short, mode = "wb")
unzip(zip_short, exdir = "data/cardio_recovery_7m30s")

files_short <- list.files("data/cardio_recovery_7m30s", pattern = "\\.csv$",
                          recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
files_short
```

```{r hrr-short-read}
# pulse.csv: heart rate in bpm; timestamps in Unix milliseconds (see README.txt)
raw_short <- read.csv("data/cardio_recovery_7m30s/pulse.csv")
head(raw_short)

time_col  <- "timestamp"   # name of the time column
hr_col    <- "value"       # name of the heart rate column
time_unit <- 1000          # timestamps are in milliseconds

short <- data.frame(time_s = raw_short[[time_col]] / time_unit,
                    hr     = raw_short[[hr_col]])
short$time_s <- short$time_s - min(short$time_s)
# remove missing and impossible values
short <- short[!is.na(short$hr) & short$hr > 30 & short$hr < 230, ]
```

The recording contains `r nrow(short)` heart rate values over `r round(max(short$time_s) / 60, 1)` minutes.

## Identification of the recovery period {#sec-hrr-short-periods}

The end of exercise is defined as the maximum of the heart rate smoothed with a running median (15 values), so that an isolated artefact cannot be selected as the peak. The recovery period goes from this peak to the end of the recording, and time is counted from the peak.

```{r hrr-short-recovery}
short$hr_smooth <- as.numeric(runmed(short$hr, k = 15))
i_peak_short  <- which.max(short$hr_smooth)
t_peak_short  <- short$time_s[i_peak_short]
hr_peak_short <- short$hr_smooth[i_peak_short]

rec_short   <- short[short$time_s >= t_peak_short, ]
rec_short$t <- rec_short$time_s - t_peak_short

# Classical indices from the literature
hrr60_short <- hr_peak_short - mean(rec_short$hr[rec_short$t >= 55 & rec_short$t <= 65])
t30_short   <- -1 / coef(lm(log(hr) ~ t, data = rec_short[rec_short$t <= 30, ]))[["t"]]
```

```{r fig-hrr-short-raw}
#| fig-cap: "Heart rate during the 7.5-minute recording (grey: raw values, red: smoothed). The dashed line marks the detected end of exercise."
#| fig-height: 3
ggplot(short, aes(time_s / 60, hr)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(aes(y = hr_smooth), colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = t_peak_short / 60, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Heart rate (bpm)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The peak is reached at t = `r round(t_peak_short)` s (HR = `r round(hr_peak_short)` bpm) and the recovery lasts `r round(max(rec_short$t) / 60, 1)` min. For comparison with the literature, HRR60 = `r round(hrr60_short, 1)` bpm [@cole1999]. T30 [@imai1994] could not be estimated reliably here (`r round(t30_short)` s): heart rate is only sampled about every 5 s and the recording starts when recovery has already begun, so the first 30 s contain very few points.

## Model fitting {#sec-hrr-short-fit}

The linear model is fitted with `lm()`, and the exponential models with `nls()` (algorithm "port", which allows us to force the amplitudes and time constants to be positive). The starting values are taken from the data: the asymptote from the mean of the last 30 values, the amplitude from the difference with the peak.

```{r hrr-short-fit}
hr_end_short <- mean(tail(rec_short$hr, 30))
amp_short    <- hr_peak_short - hr_end_short

# 1. Linear
short_lin <- lm(hr ~ t, data = rec_short)

# 2. Mono-exponential
short_mono <- nls(hr ~ hr_inf + delta * exp(-t / tau),
                  data = rec_short,
                  start = list(hr_inf = hr_end_short, delta = amp_short, tau = 60),
                  algorithm = "port", lower = c(0, 0, 1))

# 3. Bi-exponential (fast + slow phase); NULL if it does not converge
short_bi <- tryCatch(
  nls(hr ~ hr_inf + d1 * exp(-t / tau1) + d2 * exp(-t / tau2),
      data = rec_short,
      start = list(hr_inf = hr_end_short, d1 = 0.6 * amp_short, tau1 = 30,
                   d2 = 0.4 * amp_short, tau2 = 300),
      algorithm = "port", lower = c(0, 0, 1, 0, 1)),
  error = function(e) NULL)

short_models <- Filter(Negate(is.null),
                       list(Linear = short_lin, `Mono-exponential` = short_mono,
                            `Bi-exponential` = short_bi))
```

```{r tbl-hrr-short-par}
#| tbl-cap: "Fitted parameters (7.5-minute recording). Time constants in seconds, heart rate in bpm."
short_par <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(short_models), function(nm) {
  s <- summary(short_models[[nm]])$coefficients
  data.frame(Model = nm, Parameter = rownames(s), Estimate = s[, 1], SE = s[, 2])
}))
kable(short_par, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r fig-hrr-short-fits}
#| fig-cap: "Recovery data (grey) and fitted models (7.5-minute recording)."
#| fig-height: 3
short_pred <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(short_models), function(nm)
  data.frame(t = rec_short$t, hr = rec_short$hr,
             fitted = as.numeric(fitted(short_models[[nm]])),
             residual = as.numeric(residuals(short_models[[nm]])), Model = nm)))
short_pred$Model <- factor(short_pred$Model, levels = names(short_models))

ggplot(short_pred, aes(t, hr)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey70", size = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fitted, colour = Model), linewidth = 0.9) +
  labs(x = "Time since end of exercise (s)", y = "Heart rate (bpm)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Model comparison {#sec-hrr-short-comparison}

The models are compared with the goodness of fit (RMSE, $R^2$), information criteria that penalise the number of parameters (AIC, BIC; the lower the better), and the residuals, which should look like random noise around 0 if the model is adequate.

```{r tbl-hrr-short-comp}
#| tbl-cap: "Comparison of the models (7.5-minute recording)."
short_comp <- data.frame(
  Model      = names(short_models),
  Parameters = sapply(short_models, function(m) length(coef(m))),
  RMSE       = sapply(short_models, function(m) sqrt(mean(residuals(m)^2))),
  R2         = sapply(short_models, function(m)
                 1 - sum(residuals(m)^2) / sum((rec_short$hr - mean(rec_short$hr))^2)),
  AIC        = sapply(short_models, AIC),
  BIC        = sapply(short_models, BIC),
  row.names  = NULL)
short_best <- short_comp$Model[which.min(short_comp$AIC)]
kable(short_comp, digits = 3)
```

```{r fig-hrr-short-residuals}
#| fig-cap: "Residuals of the models as a function of time (7.5-minute recording)."
#| fig-height: 3.5
ggplot(short_pred, aes(t, residual)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ Model, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time since end of exercise (s)", y = "Residual (bpm)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r hrr-short-ftest}
# Is the bi-exponential significantly better than the mono-exponential?
if (!is.null(short_bi)) anova(short_mono, short_bi)
```

## Results for this recording {#sec-hrr-short-results}

The linear model has the largest error (RMSE = `r round(short_comp$RMSE[short_comp$Model == "Linear"], 2)` bpm) and its residuals are clearly structured (@fig-hrr-short-residuals): the decrease of heart rate is not constant over time. The mono-exponential model gives a time constant $\tau$ = `r round(coef(short_mono)[["tau"]], 1)` s and an asymptote of `r round(coef(short_mono)[["hr_inf"]], 1)` bpm.

The bi-exponential model has a slightly lower AIC, but not a lower BIC, and its parameters cannot be interpreted physiologically: its "slow" time constant (`r round(max(coef(short_bi)[c("tau1", "tau2")]))` s) is much longer than the recording, its asymptote drops to `r round(coef(short_bi)[["hr_inf"]], 1)` bpm, and the standard errors are huge (@tbl-hrr-short-par). The second component only describes a slow drift over 7.5 minutes, which the data cannot distinguish from the asymptote. Following H4, the added complexity is not justified: the **mono-exponential** model is the best description of this recording, on which only one recovery phase can be observed.
